whatItIs: Nootropics Depot Lion's Mane Extract is a single-ingredient supplement providing standardised Hericium erinaceus fruiting body extract at 500mg per capsule. Nootropics Depot is widely regarded as the most rigorous quality-focused retailer in the US nootropics market, operating an ISO-certified in-house testing laboratory and publishing a Certificate of Analysis (CoA) for every batch. For GCC buyers: as a single-ingredient product, it presents a simpler customs profile than multi-ingredient stacks; the publicly available CoA can be provided to SFDA, MOHAP, or relevant MOH authorities if documentation is requested. The product is caffeine-free, is vegan per the brand's product page (capsule shell material not stated, checked 2026-10-07), and ships from the US.
howItWorks: Lion's Mane fruiting body contains hericenones, compounds that cross the blood-brain barrier and stimulate Nerve Growth Factor (NGF) synthesis. NGF promotes neuronal survival, axon growth, and maintenance of neurons in the hippocampus and cortex -- the regions responsible for learning and memory. Nootropics Depot uses a standardised fruiting body extract rather than mycelium (which has a lower hericenone content). The result is a more potent and consistent NGF stimulus per capsule.
whatToExpect: Lion's Mane is a long-game supplement. Expect no acute effects on day one. At 4 weeks: some users report slightly clearer thinking and improved mental endurance. At 8-12 weeks: measurable improvements in memory and neuroprotective markers in studies. For best results, take consistently every day with a fat-containing meal (hericenones are fat-soluble). This product is best combined with a multi-ingredient stack (e.g. Mind Lab Pro already contains Lion's Mane) rather than used as a standalone primary supplement.

whatItIs: Eu Yan Sang is a 145-year-old Traditional Chinese Medicine company founded in 1879, headquartered in Singapore with 200+ retail locations across Asia-Pacific. BrainMAX+ is their modern cognitive health product featuring Cera-Q — a silk fibroin protein extract with one citable 3-week trial in healthy adults averaging about 55 (Kang 2018, maker-affiliated authors) showing higher memory-test scores at 400–600mg/day (the trial tested 280–600mg). The formula bridges TCM heritage (Goji Berry, Chinese Wild Ginseng) with modern peptide science. For GCC buyers: the product is sold on Eu Yan Sang's Singapore e-commerce storefront; we could not confirm delivery terms to GCC addresses in our 2026-09-28 check. It is sold as powder sachets (3g x 30 per box, one sachet daily per the product page), not capsules, and is caffeine-free.
howItWorks: Cera-Q (silk fibroin protein hydrolysate) has no established mechanism in human studies; the one 3-week trial we could cite reported dose-dependent gains on a memory quotient, learning gradient and recall measures at 400–600mg/day (the trial tested 280–600mg). Goji Berry extract provides antioxidant neuroprotection via zeaxanthin and betaine compounds — Goji is a staple in TCM with centuries of documented use. Chinese Wild Ginseng contains ginsenosides that modulate NMDA receptor activity and support cerebral blood flow.
whatToExpect: BrainMAX+ comes as powder sachets dissolved in water. The one Cera-Q trial we could cite measured memory after 3 weeks; it did not measure mental clarity or onset. Weeks 4-8: cumulative memory and concentration benefits from the ginseng and goji combination. At about $54.71 USD per 30-sachet box (S$69.90) it is priced as a premium product.
pros: Cera-Q has a placebo-controlled memory trial (3 weeks, maker-affiliated)
cons: Korea's food regulator (MFDS) revoked Cera-Q's functional-ingredient recognition in November 2017 after its supporting mouse study was retracted for data fabrication (retraction notice: J Microbiol Biotechnol, Dec 2016); in Korea it is sold as a general food (per Yang & Chung 2026, Food Supplements and Biomaterials for Health, and Sisa Journal, Feb 2020).
